read the roles claim of the verified access token in the gateway and load it into the security context as authorities, then make every /resume endpoint candidate-only with a @HasRole annotation, a meta-annotation over @PreAuthorize, answering 403 with the error envelope. remove the round-trip to the app-backend that used to read the caller to check their user type, keeping the fetch only where the flow needs the profile image. with unit tests

make the gateway bounce early the relayed requests whose role is already known to be wrong: a filter after the signature verification with a table of exact method plus path templates for the routes that belong to one kind of user, answering 403 with the error envelope. it is an optimization, not the enforcement point, so anything the table does not cover is relayed untouched and the app-backend keeps deciding. use exact templates rather than prefixes, since the supported languages endpoint hangs off the candidate-only resume path and must stay open. with unit tests
now that the supported resume languages endpoint downstream is candidate-only, add it to the relayed routes the gateway bounces early for a caller without the candidate role

relay the browser's lynq-iam auth calls through the gateway so the frontend has a single origin: map POST /auth/register, POST /auth/login/username, POST /auth/login/email, POST /auth/refresh, GET /auth/check-username, GET /auth/check-email and PATCH /auth/update-password to a new feign client against the lynq-iam base url, relaying method, path, query string, headers, body and status unchanged and injecting no user-id header, since lynq-iam reads the credential it is handed rather than a header. open only those exact paths and verbs in the public path rules: anonymous for the logins, the registration and the availability checks; header-required but signature-exempt for the refresh, whose bearer credential is the opaque refresh token and not a jwt; unchanged for the password update, which carries an access token. leave /auth/validate and /auth/user-info out of the allowlist so they answer 404, and keep the request uuid header required everywhere. with unit and e2e tests

the relayed lynq-ml endpoints are cut at 60 seconds and answer 502 while lynq-ml is still generating: the feign read timeout raised for the typed lynqMl client does not reach the relay client, because feign resolves that config by client name and the relay one is lynqMlDmz. give it the same 10s connect and 310s read timeout in both profiles, so skill-enhance on a slow local model finishes instead of failing at the gateway

map the agent's 409 responses into the gateway envelope without dropping the code, so the browser can tell TURN_IN_PROGRESS, CONVERSATION_EXHAUSTED and ALREADY_APPLIED apart, and relay its 403 and 404 as themselves instead of a generic 502

add LYNQ_AGENT_URL to the service config in both Helm values files, pointing at the in-cluster agent service, so the deployed gateway does not depend on the compiled-in default either

stop naming the caller by id to the services behind the gateway.
